target_applications: domestic/professional service, healthcare and rehabilitation assistance, HRI research

base_type.value: two driving wheels (diff-drive) + 3 pivoting 75 mm castors

torso_lift.value: extensible torso, 200 mm travel: height 1.15-1.35 m (current website claims up to 1.45 m — conflicting)

actuators.value: electric joints with overload safety clutches; series-elastic actuators in hands; active force-torque control

end_effector.value: 2x underactuated hands, 4 DoF / 2 DoA, distributed pressure skin, ~20 N tip force, door-opening design

sensors_head.value: 2-DoF head: OV580 twin camera module, XtionPro Live RGB-D, 2 mics, speaker, RGB LED matrix face

sensors_wrist_hand.value: 2x 6-axis F/T sensors in arms; pressure-sensitive skin on hands; IMUs in motor boards for impact detection

compute.value: 2x Nano-ITX i7 PCs + MYIR Xilinx Z-turn board; onboard 5 GHz Wi-Fi AP

software_stack.value: open-source YARP middleware (iCub ecosystem), ROS bridge, Gazebo/RViz; assistive-rehab framework

safety_compliance.value: safe-HRI design: joint safety clutches, compliant control, closed covers, e-stop conforming to ISO 13482 (function-level claim, no certification found)

price.value: target 'cost of a small family car' (~EUR 20-30k class, estimated); never sold at volume

availability.value: research distribution only (IIT-built units, travel case orderable); not a commercial product

deployment_evidence.value: rehabilitation-assistant trials with Fondazione Don Gnocchi (assistive-rehab joint lab); HR1 healthcare assistant publication 2022; still operational at IIT 20th anniversary Dec 2023

notes: Discovery note said torso 1.15-1.35 m (matches official spec PDF); IIT website currently says up to 1.45 m and 1.5 kg payload fully extended — treated as conflicting later claim. Body ~50% polymer for cost. IIT humanoid focus now on legged ergoCub (excluded).
